key_insight: A mixed-primal FEM couples fourth-order solvent electrostatics with a second-order solute model, enabling accurate field and Maxwell stress approximation with parameter-robust error bounds.
engineering_relevance: Accurate electrostatic stress and interaction-force calculations support simulations of ionic solutions and electrolyte–solute interfaces.
method: Introduce potential-gradient, divergence, and divergence-gradient variables in the solvent.
Retain a primal solute formulation to enforce transmission conditions without Lagrange multipliers.
Discretise vector fields with Raviart–Thomas elements and scalar fields with piecewise polynomials.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments in 2D and 3D validate theoretical convergence rates, including optimal postprocessed Maxwell stress convergence on quasi-uniform meshes except for the lowest-order 3D scheme.
watch_item: Unresolved parameter-dependent length scales can reduce convergence by up to half an order, and boundary layers may still make solution regularity parameter-dependent.
paper_title: A mixed-primal FEM for Poisson-Fermi interfacial problems
